name: intmap-ops
description: IntMap — a Vite-built static site (#R175) plus the operational quality baseline around it (CI, static checks, browser smoke tests, internal-QA runner, release/rollback/monitoring tooling). `dependencies` are what the browser ships; `devDependencies` are build/CI only.

scripts.//serve: (#R175) `serve` still means 'give me the real site on 4173' as the standing docs say — it just builds first now. `preview` skips the build when dist/ is already current; `dev` is the HMR loop.
scripts.serve: npm run build && node scripts/serve.mjs --root dist
scripts.//check:engine: (#R178) the renderer-decoupling gate: only js/geo-engine.js may name MapLibre. Parses, so a comment mentioning `map.` never trips it.
scripts.//check:i18n: (#R239) the ONE translation gate — every language against every surface it can be translated on (keyed table wherever it is declared, the inline L() table, the five positional arguments, the two reading pages, and the data-i18n keys the markup asks for). `--todo <code>` prints the commands that close a gap. Runs inside `npm test`.
scripts.//check:docs: the cross-document gate: the facts written down in more than one place (what is served, how many Edge Functions there are, which languages exist, how production is deployed) are compared with the repository AND with each other. It also enforces that Architecture.md stays a current-state spec rather than a changelog.
scripts.//check:companies: (#R354) the company-atlas gate. data/companies/ is built from Wikidata, OpenStreetMap, SEC EDGAR and GLEIF, and the builder is written to DROP anything it cannot source — this proves it did. Twenty checks, numbered the same way in docs/COMPANIES.md §7: no money value without a currency and a period, no facility without a source and a stated position precision, no 0,0 coordinate, no duplicate id, and the nineteen companies the brief names must still resolve to their own identity. `--report` prints the coverage table.
scripts.//check:agents: (#R503) the agent-context gate. The standing instructions live in AGENTS.md (both products read it), and the round procedure, the execution strategy and the five roles live under .agents/ — provider-neutral. scripts/agent-sync.mjs RENDERS those into .claude/agents, .claude/skills and .codex/agents, because each product only reads its own location; this re-renders and compares, so editing a copy fails instead of creating a second 正本. It also measures AGENTS.md against Codex project_doc_max_bytes (32,768): MEASURED #R503 that the overflow is dropped silently — the head of the file loads and the tail does not.
scripts.//build:countryfacts: (#R453) restcountries.com was withdrawn — every /v3.1 and /v5 path 301s to a 261-byte deprecation notice whose redirect carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, so `enrichCountry()` failed on every country card and `catch(e){}` made that look exactly like a country with no neighbours. The six facts it supplied are built in now: mledoze/countries (REST Countries' own upstream, ODbL) for capital / currency / languages / land borders / UN membership / demonym, and the IANA time-zone database for standard-time offsets, keyed by the code js/countries-ui.js itself derives. NOT a gate and NOT in `npm test` — it needs the network; the committed file is checked offline by tests/r453-checks.test.mjs and the rows are checked ON THE SCREEN by tests/r424.spec.js. `--check` re-derives and compares.
scripts.//build:coastline: (#R495) 「海から200km以上」 had no measurement anywhere in the program. This builds data/coastline.json.gz from Natural Earth 1:10m physical `coastline`, simplified to a 2 km tolerance and split into the world OCEAN (`coords`) and the landlocked seas the same layer carries (`enclosed` — the Caspian, 12 parts, measured). NOT a gate and NOT in `npm test`: it downloads 60 MB of GeoJSON, and a CI runner has no cache for it — the committed artefact is checked OFFLINE by tests/r495-checks.test.mjs, which also re-derives every distance with a second, different spherical formula. `--check` re-derives and compares.
scripts.//build:rail: (#R388) OpenStreetMap の全世界鉄道。掃引はセル単位でキャッシュするので再開可能——2回目以降のビルドはネットワークに触らない。
scripts.build:rail: node scripts/rail/fetch.mjs && node --max-old-space-size=8192 scripts/rail/build.mjs && node scripts/rail/stations.mjs
scripts.//check:catalog: (#R278) the Atlas catalogue gate: every capability the dispatch in js/atlas-console.js can execute must be described to the planner in function SYS(). An action the catalogue does not describe does not exist for the planner (#R115) — six of them, the road-network isochrone included, were invisible until this gate was written. Runs inside `npm test`.
scripts.//check:wars: (#R381) scripts/build-wars.mjs shipped in #R349 with a --check mode and NOTHING THAT RAN IT, so the committed data/wars.json could drift from the record in scripts/wars/ and no gate would notice. It re-derives the file and compares it byte for byte, and it runs the whole self-audit on the way: the gazetteer cross-check, the CShapes date check, the cut check, the named-city control checks (#R409 added the sixteen spans where only `control` describes a country a front otherwise divides — the count moves whenever the record does, so it is not written here) and the unused-anchor check.
scripts.//check:histcities: (#R427/#R521) the historical CITY-name record. data/hist-cities.json is re-derived from scripts/histcities/ and compared byte for byte, and the whole self-audit runs on the way. ⚠ #R521 replaced BOTH halves of what that audit asks. It used to resolve every key against data/gazetteer-world.json.gz — a file the news locator builds by keeping `the more populous homonym` and dropping the rest, so the uniqueness it was asked to prove had been imposed on its evidence, and 1950 relabelled 高知市 コーチン. The evidence is now data/histcities-homonyms.json.gz (GeoNames cities500, unfiltered, restricted to the record’s own spellings), and the rule is no longer «this spelling is unique on Earth» but «this spelling is bound to this point»: every row carries a guard radius derived as half the distance to its nearest namesake, the coordinate must be within 10 km of the settlement GeoNames holds under that spelling, and a namesake inside the guard needs a { key, place, cc, why } waiver that this build re-tests every run.
scripts.//check:cshapes: (#R700) data/cshapes.js — the 5.6 MB the time machine answers the whole of 1886-2019 with, the outlines the two world-war layers are cut from, and the yardstick check:histborders derives its own floor against — WAS THE ONLY BORDER RECORD WITH NO BUILD AND NO GATE. Nothing could say where its bytes came from and, the reason this round opened, nothing said what shipping them costs: the upstream is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which makes credit a CONDITION of redistribution, and the row that named it carried no licence at all (the #R689 shape). ⚠ LIKE ITS NEIGHBOURS IT RE-DERIVES NOTHING: the upstream is 26.3 MB from a university web server that refused three of this round's connections outright, so it proves the committed bytes instead — every ring closed, on the globe and referenced (the six that are not are #R142/#R146's superseded German rings, counted and ratcheted rather than forgiven), every record nine slots with an ordered span inside the window js/time-borders.js READS OUT OF THE APP rather than restates, one name per Gleditsch-Ward code and no code drawn twice on one day, the credit paid by a js/reference-data.js row that carries the licence text and the publisher's citation as VALUES, and — the part that is not structural — data/hist-borders.js's declared floor re-derived from this file, because that bundle's window is a function of this one's smallest and largest world. The rebuild itself (`node scripts/build-cshapes.mjs`) reproduces 1,985 of 1,991 rings byte for byte and deliberately writes nothing: five records, the two Germanys 1945-2019, are #R145/#R146's geometry and not the upstream's.
scripts.//check:histeras: (#R679) data/hist-eras.js — 53 world snapshots, 17 of them BC — held to its own invariants. ⚠ ITS NAMES ARE NO LONGER PART OF THIS GATE: #R686 put them here because the table answered for this bundle alone, and #R695 made one table answer for all three border records, so the names have their own gate (check:histnames) whose subject is the table rather than any one bundle.
scripts.//check:histnames: (#R695) data/histnames.json — the ONE historical-name table, held to the three records it answers for. A name it localizes must be a name one of those records actually draws, a QID it answers must be one data/hist-borders.js states, and a language nobody wrote may not be claimed. ⚠ IT HAS TWO STRENGTHS: where the Wikidata harvest cache exists it REBUILDS and compares; on a machine without one (CI) it measures the shipped file alone and says so — the first version failed on its own absence rather than on the bytes, which is the same problem every neighbouring historical gate solves by re-deriving nothing at all. It is its own gate because its subject is the NAME, not any one bundle: #R686 measured 18.6-38.0% of cshapes localized against 57.5-87.1% of hist-borders, and the difference was which upstream happened to write name:xx.
scripts.//check:histadmin: (#R680) THE TWO LARGEST BUNDLES IN data/ — data/hist-admin1.js (11.1 MB, 4,839 first-level units) and data/hist-admin2.js (19.4 MB, 22,708 second-level ones) — had NO GATE AT ALL: 30.5 MB from which the map draws every province and district line, every label on one, every answer to a click on one and every coverage count, and neither `npm test` nor CI weighed a byte of it. All four neighbouring historical bundles have one; these two were written after those gates and were never given one. Like check:histborders and check:histeras it RE-DERIVES NOTHING (the build consumes OHM's whole admin_level 3-6 extract, 28,211 relations, measured 3.4 GB of Overpass on one resumed run) and proves the committed bytes instead: that each file defines the one global its own NAME implies and no other — the #R604 accident, where the deeper tier shipped as `window.__HISTADM1=` and replaced the first tier's record on load — that it holds the admin levels its name implies, that every ring closes and is on the globe and is referenced by some unit, that every ring index resolves, that every span is ordered and reachable, that every unit carries a unique OpenHistoricalMap relation id (which is what makes a click sharp, #R669), and that EVERY CENTURY the bundle claims to reach has something in force. The tiers are discovered from data/, not listed, so a third one is checked the day it is added. The residual it cannot see is stated in docs/TESTING.md.
scripts.//build:histcities-homonyms: (#R521) the evidence check:histcities judges against — for every spelling in scripts/histcities/, EVERY GeoNames cities500 settlement answering to it in its name, its ASCII name or its untagged alternate list, with no population sort, no dedup, no stop-words and no length floor. NOT a gate and NOT in `npm test`: it downloads 13.6 MB from GeoNames and a CI runner has no cache for it. The committed artefact is checked offline — build-hist-cities fails on any key the index does not cover, and tests/r427-checks ⑧ asserts the index still CARRIES the three collisions the old oracle had deleted. Re-run it whenever the record gains a spelling.
scripts.//check:languages: (#R538) THE LANGUAGE LAYER HAD NO GATE AT ALL, and the thing it needed one for is exactly what went wrong: scripts/build-culture.mjs resolved Factbook prose through a hand table of 119 regular expressions and SILENTLY DROPPED whatever the table did not recognise, so the country was coloured by the next language down — Burkina Faso shipped as Fula 7.8% with Mossi 52.9% missing, Namibia as Afrikaans 9.4% behind Oshiwambo 49.7%, Mozambique as Portuguese 16.6% behind Makhuwa 26.1%, and 3,136 tests were green. This runs offline over the shipped files and asserts what no test asserted: that every Glottocode a country names exists in data/language-tree.json and has a name; that `top` IS the largest measured share rather than merely looking like one; that a country with no measured share says so instead of naming its first-listed language; that the tree is a tree (every parent resolves, no cycles, no duplicate codes); and that every row of the resolution ledger data/language-aliases.json points somewhere and has a written reason. Runs inside `npm test`.
scripts.//check:perf: (#R311) THE STARTUP BUDGET, and before it nothing in CI weighed a single byte of the deploy — `vite build` printed «Some chunks are larger than 3000 kB» on every run and exited 0. It reads .perf/build-report.json (written by the build itself, scripts/build-report.mjs) and judges the two halves separately: the EAGER set is ratcheted in BOTH directions (over the ceiling is a regression; well under it means the ceiling stopped asserting anything and must be lowered with --update, the same rule #R194 gave the test-time budget), while ASYNC chunks and the dist/ totals get a ceiling only, because a 4.8 MB Cesium chunk a MapLibre session never fetches is not a startup cost. Needs a build first, so it runs as its own CI step after `npm run build` rather than inside `npm test` (which already builds once, in the browser half, concurrently).
scripts.//check:assets: (#R322) THE OTHER HALF OF THE DEPLOY. check:perf weighs what Rollup produced; this weighs what was COPIED — data/ is 55.8 MB of a 105.7 MB tree and none of it passes through the bundler. Every file in dist/ is matched against the strings the source actually contains (js/ src/ css/ *.html sw.js, plus the small manifests under data/ that name assets the JavaScript never spells out), and a file nothing mentions, a payload shipped twice, or a file over the per-file ceiling with no recorded reason fails the gate. Needs a build first, so it runs beside check:perf rather than inside npm test.
scripts.//perf:report: (#R311) the same measurement without the judging — eager vs async, raw/gzip/brotli, the largest eager modules, duplicated modules. `npm run build` writes it; this prints it.
scripts.//master: (#R282) the master copy is the OneDrive working directory (AGENTS.md §6), and until this existed no step in the workflow was responsible for it: a round could merge, deploy and back up to USB while OneDrive stayed fifteen commits behind. `master:sync` is the last step of every task; `master:check` is the gate the USB mirror runs first. NOT in `npm test` — on a CI runner the checkout is a detached PR ref and 'behind origin/main' is the correct state there. What CI can prove about the rule is in tests/r282-checks.test.mjs.
scripts.//setup:codex: (#R704) the machine-local half of «Codex と同じ使用感». The repository half — AGENTS.md plus .agents/ rendered into .claude/ and .codex/ — is gated by check:agents; ~/.codex/config.toml is OUTSIDE the repository and holds the four facts that gate cannot reach. MEASURED #R704: [hooks.state] was EMPTY, i.e. the SessionStart hook this repo ships had never run in Codex at all, so no Codex session ever received the branch/round line or the one memory store #R696 built; model_reasoning_effort was low; neither approval_policy nor sandbox_mode was set; and the memory store, the handoff cursors and every round worktree sit outside any workspace, so workspace-write could not write them until they were named. Deliberately NOT a check:* gate: it measures THIS machine and a CI runner has no ~/.codex — what CI can prove about it is in tests/r704-codex-parity-seamless-checks.test.mjs.
scripts.//test:profile: (#R184) the renderer PROFILING instrument — frame time beside a sharpness measure, swept over the anti-aliasing and LOD settings. Excluded from the default run (see playwright.config.js): it is a measurement, not a gate.
scripts.//test:profile2: (#R191) …and it STILL did not run. On Windows spawnSync('npx.cmd') without a shell cannot resolve the launcher, so it returned status null, `||0` turned that into a clean exit, and the command printed nothing at all and reported success — the same silence #R190 set out to fix, one layer down. `shell` on win32 makes the launcher resolvable, and a null status is now a FAILURE rather than a pass. Verified by running it: 1 passed (2.8m), with the sweep table on stdout.
scripts.//test:seq: (#R205) the same steps in the old sequential order, for when an interleaved log is in the way of reading a failure.
scripts.test:seq: node scripts/static-checks.mjs && node scripts/engine-coupling.mjs --gate && node scripts/atlas-catalog.mjs --check && node scripts/companies-audit.mjs --gate && node scripts/build-wars.mjs --check && node scripts/build-hist-cities.mjs --check && node scripts/test-budget.mjs && npm run test:checks && node scripts/run-tests.mjs && node scripts/perf-budget.mjs
scripts.//test:deep: (#R203) the half of the suite that does NOT stand in front of a push. (#R372) MEASURED: the deep tier is 105 spec files against the core tier's 7 — and the number written here said 59, docs/TESTING.md said 64 and scripts/worktree.mjs said 27, all at the same time; (#R500) three of the four copies had drifted apart AGAIN (86 here / 92 in docs/TESTING.md / 82 in scripts/worktree.mjs) and `deep-tier-size` in scripts/doc-facts.mjs now measures every one of them; it is derived, so re-measure with `node -e "import('./scripts/tiers.mjs').then(t=>console.log(t.tierSpecs('deep').length))"` rather than trusting this sentence, because #R204/#R207 turned the split from a list into a PRICE (scripts/tiers.mjs, CORE_MAX_S) — a spec stands in the gate only if it costs at most one second, so nearly every per-round file is deep. Locally 89 of them run at two workers and the five `solo` Cesium files then run at one; scripts/test-budget.mjs measures the whole suite at __MIN__ min of serial browser time. It runs NIGHTLY (ci.yml `schedule`) and on demand, NOT on push (#R207). Run it before opening a PR that touches 3-D, Cesium, the simulators or the physics. `test:all` is both. ⚠ scripts/tiers.mjs derives the split; tests/durations.json supplies the measured seconds and the `solo` list, not a `deep` list. ⚠ When it goes red nobody is watching by default — scripts/deep-alarm.mjs opens an issue and `node scripts/worktree.mjs status` prints last night's verdict (#R304).
scripts.//check:testbudget: (#R197) the suite has a CEILING and it only ever goes down — see scripts/test-budget.mjs. A round that adds test time must take at least as much out somewhere else; that is what stops the per-round spec files accumulating into 「何重にも」.
scripts.//prebuild: (#R232) js/locales/_langs.js is the language list for the two static reading pages (no bundler there, so no import.meta.glob). Regenerating it here is what makes 「adding a language = adding one locale file」 true for those pages too; tests/r232-checks fails if the committed copy is stale.
